title: Simulation of Register Increment
statement: Let $A$ be a register-program instruction map with initial label $l_0$, let the oracle assign a Boolean answer to each decider and bit string, and let $x$ be an input bit string. Suppose labels $l,l'$ and a register $r$ satisfy $A(l)=\operatorname{inc}(r,l')$. For any register valuation $v$ and output word, if the length of the binary expansion of $v(r)+1$ is at most the integer bound $W$, then the compiled program simulates this increment from the configuration with label $l$ and valuation $v$ to the configuration with label $l'$ and valuation obtained by replacing $v(r)$ by $v(r)+1$, preserving the input and output; throughout the simulation, every intermediate configuration before the endpoint has no pending oracle call and all work-head positions lie between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: An instruction map A and initial label l₀
An oracle assigning Boolean answers by decider and bit string
Labels l and l′, register r, and A(l) = inc(r,l′)
